author: Figes, Orlando
title: A People's Tragedy: The Russian Revolution, 1891–1924
notes: The narrative backbone for the 1917 pack: a social and cultural history arguing that the revolution was made from below by the collapse of Russian civil society rather than by a party. Strong on the countryside, on individual lives followed across the whole period, and on why February and October are two different kinds of event. Written against the Soviet account and against the coup thesis alike, and its judgements on the Bolsheviks are severe. Not readable at page level from this project's environment (the Internet Archive copy is borrow-only), so citations to it carry no pages.
